I need to respond to a trade offer in Monopoly.

I'm p3 with Tennessee and Illinois. p4 offers $200 for my Tennessee. I'm weighing this against my plan to swap Illinois for New York to complete the orange set.

This trade is a clear loss. p4 would gain two-thirds of the orange set and a major advantage. I will reject it.

I'm weighing whether to counter or reject outright. The original Illinois-for-New-York swap is dead. I'll likely keep Tennessee and aim for New York or St. James instead.

I'm now considering a counter offer of cash for New York. That would give me two-thirds of the orange set and only St. James left to complete it.

Offering cash for New York would still give me two-thirds of the orange set, so p4 would likely refuse. I'm now calculating whether paying $400–$500 for New York is worth it, since an orange monopoly is the strongest early advantage. After buying New York and St. James, I'd have roughly $374 left to build houses.

Three houses on each orange property cost $900. With only $374 left, I can only afford one house per property. That yields solid but not decisive rent. The orange monopoly is too expensive to build right now.

I'll reject the trade outright. I'm now considering a counter offer of $350 for New York, since p4 already owns two-thirds of the orange set and could buy St. James next turn.
